title: Decide how this configuration uses the Spoons once they move here
description:
The configuration in ~/.config/Hammerspoon2 loads the Spoons from its own Spoons/ directory, and so does hs_interactive-gt's use(). Once the Spoons move into this repository, decide how the configuration gets them, without breaking it:

1. Install them from the published repository with hs.spoons.install(), like any user.
2. Or keep working copies, for example by linking each <name>.spoon2 into Spoons/<name>. A link is allowed locally, although an installed Spoon may not contain one.

Also decide what happens to ../Spoons afterwards. lib/ stays there, because init.js, hs_jp-gt, hs_hass-gt and hs_url-gt use lib/shell.js, and init.js and hs_jp-gt use lib/authinfo.js. The parent repository has uncommitted changes in hs_kanata-gt and hs_emacs-gt, which must be committed before anything is moved.
acceptance_criteria: The user has reviewed the result and approved closing this bead.

title: Write the pattern a Spoon uses to depend on another Spoon
description:
Hammerspoon 2 has no notion of dependencies between Spoons (see ai/hs2-spoon-install.org). Write the code a Spoon uses to load another one:

1. Load it with hs.spoons.load() and catch ENOTINSTALLED.
2. Then either install it from this repository with hs.spoons.install(), or fail with a message that names the missing Spoon and gives the line that installs it. Decide with the user which of these to do, and whether to ask first.
3. Decide where the code lives: copied into each Spoon that needs it, or in a small Spoon of its own. A library Spoon would itself be a dependency.

Also handle the cycle between hs_interactive-gt and hs_menu-gt, which each refer to the other. Record the dependencies between all the Spoons in one table.
acceptance_criteria: The user has reviewed the result and approved closing this bead.

title: Decide the repository layout and conventions for published Spoons
description:
Decide how this repository is laid out, following ai/hs2-spoon-install.org:

1. Whether Spoons are <name>.spoon2 directories at the top level or inside Spoons/.
2. What every Spoon contains: spoon.json, init.js, readme, and a directory for screenshots.
3. Which files are kept out of a Spoon, such as __pycache__ and test output, since installing any Spoon downloads the whole repository.
4. What to do with large data files, such as the 2.7 MB kanji data in hs_kanji-gt, which everyone downloads with any Spoon.
5. The format of the readme (org or Markdown). GitHub shows both, but Markdown is what most users expect.

Record the decisions in this repository's CLAUDE.md, so that later Spoons follow them.
acceptance_criteria: The user has reviewed the result and approved closing this bead.
notes:
Requirement added by the user on 2026-11-14: nothing local to the user's machine may be in a published Spoon; a Spoon from which it cannot be removed is not published. Record this rule in CLAUDE.md with the layout decisions.
Decided on 2026-11-14 with the recommendations accepted: Spoons/<name>.spoon2/; spoon.json, init.js, readme.md, images/ plus runtime files; export-ignore for developer and planning files; images at display size; Markdown readmes; version raised on every change. Recorded in CLAUDE.md under Publishing Spoons. .gitattributes and .gitignore added; git archive --worktree-attributes HEAD leaves only readme.org, so export-ignore works locally. Whether GitHub's zip honours it is checked after the first push.

title: Document how Hammerspoon 2 installs Spoons
description: Read hs.spoons in the Hammerspoon 2 source and record how a Spoon is found in a repository, validated, installed, loaded and updated, and what this means for how this repository is laid out and how Spoons depend on each other.
acceptance_criteria: The findings are written up with references to the source. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Written to ai/hs2-spoon-install.org. Main points: a repository's Spoons must be <name>.spoon2 directories at the top level or in Spoons/; spoon.json needs name, author, version and description; no symlinks; hs.spoons has no dependency mechanism; update() only reinstalls when the version changes. Also found while answering the user: the published Spoons do not need lib/shell.js, whose original reason (upstream #267) is fixed; only commandRunInput lacks an hs.task equivalent.
close_reason: Findings in ai/hs2-spoon-install.org; approved by user

title: Publish the general-use Spoons as an installable collection
description:
Move the Spoons in ../Spoons into this repository and publish it, so that anyone can install them with Hammerspoon 2's hs.spoons.install() or hs.spoons.use().

The work has six parts:

1. Lay out the repository so that hs.spoons.install() finds each Spoon. Each Spoon must be a directory named <name>.spoon2, at the top level or in a Spoons directory.
2. Remove everything local to the user's machine from each Spoon. A Spoon from which something local cannot be removed is not published.
3. Make each Spoon useful on its own. Code shared through ../lib has to be packaged so that a single installed Spoon still works. A Spoon that needs another one must check for it, and either offer to install it or fail with a message that says what is missing.
4. Review each Spoon for workarounds that were written because Hammerspoon 2 lacked a feature it now has.
5. Rewrite the documentation for users. It should explain what each Spoon does for the user, with screenshots where they help, and list the Spoons in order of how likely a user is to want them.
6. Check that every Spoon installs and loads the way a user would install it, and then publish.
acceptance_criteria: Every published Spoon contains nothing local to the user's machine, installs from the published repository with hs.spoons.install(), loads on its own or with its declared dependencies, and is documented for users. The user has approved closing this epic.

title: Analyze AeroSpace as an alternative for spaces
description:
AeroSpace (https://github.com/nikitabobko/AeroSpace) is another window manager for macOS. Analyze it as an alternative to yabai and to upstream hs.spaces (pull request #371), using the same questions this epic has asked of yabai. Check the following, and verify each from its documentation or source rather than from memory:

1. What AeroSpace's workspaces are. Find out whether they are macOS Spaces or its own, and what that means for Mission Control and for other applications.
2. Whether it needs System Integrity Protection disabled, and which permissions it needs.
3. How a client talks to it. Find out whether it has a socket, what the protocol is, and whether a client can receive events without running a shell command for each one.
4. How it names workspaces, and whether names survive a restart. This matters because the Spoon identifies spaces by name.
5. Which of the functions in hs_yabai-gt/ai/hs1-spaces.org and the adopted features in yabai-extras.org it provides.
6. Its license, how it is maintained, and whether it works on macOS 27.
7. Whether it can be used without tiling, since tiling was left out of this epic.

Write the analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai, and end it with a comparison of yabai, AeroSpace and hs.spaces from #371. Do not install AeroSpace without asking the user first.

notes: Analysis in hs_yabai-gt/ai/aerospace.org, from the clone at ~/git.w/AeroSpace (commit 6ed6af62). AeroSpace emulates workspaces by moving hidden windows off-screen instead of using macOS Spaces; needs no SIP; its socket keeps connections open, has a documented protocol and a subscribe command that streams events as JSON; workspace names persist in its config. title: Record findings on yabai's socket, its license, and upstream hs.spaces
description:
While discussing the evaluation in eqg.3, several findings came up that change the direction of the epic. Record them in hs_yabai-gt/ai:

1. yabai's socket answers one request per connection and never writes to a client, so events reach a client only through a shell command run by a signal. A measurement showed that a request over the socket costs far less than running yabai -m as a process.
2. yabai and Hammerspoon 2 are both under the MIT license.
3. Hammerspoon 2 already has hs.socket, which supports Unix domain sockets, and hs.window already uses a private SkyLight function.
4. Upstream Hammerspoon 2 has an open pull request, #371, that ports hs.spaces from Hammerspoon 1 without needing SIP disabled, and an issue, #86, about switching spaces with synthesized swipes. The pull request lacks moving a window to a space and instant switching, both of which yabai has.
acceptance_criteria: The findings are written up in hs_yabai-gt/ai with their sources. The user has approved closing this bead.
notes: Written: the socket's one-request behaviour, the cost measurement and the events section in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org; the licenses, hs.socket, PR #371 and issue #86 in hs_yabai-gt/ai/upstream-hs-spaces.org. Question 1 of eqg.3 is answered there: hs.socket supports Unix domain sockets.

title: Evaluate whether a Spoon can talk to yabai over its socket
description:

2. Which commands fail without the scripting addition? System Integrity Protection stays enabled, so the scripting addition is not loaded. Test this rather than relying on the fork's readme.
3. How can space change events reach Hammerspoon 2? yabai reports events by running a shell command registered as a signal. Find something that Hammerspoon 2 can receive directly, and avoid polling.
4. Do yabai's window identifiers match those of HSWindow?

The Spoon's name is already decided: hs_yabai-gt. The report ends with a recommendation to go ahead or to stop, and a list of the beads that the implementation needs, if those differ from the ones already filed. Record what is learned in hs_yabai-gt/ai/yabai.org.
